repos.name: apr-emu-updater
repos.description: PS5 payload that keeps APR Emu up to date on installed titles, from a web interface on the console.
repos.readme: # APR Emu Updater v2.0.6 Some games on a jailbroken ps5 rely on a file called **APR Emu** (`libSceAmpr.sprx`). Different games run best with different versions of it, and swapping that file by hand means editing game images. This payload does it for you. It opens a small web page on your ps5 where every installed game is listed with the APR Emu version it is currently using, and you pick the version each game should use. > [!IMPORTANT] > Despite its name, **APR Emu Updater does not update APR Emu itself**. It > chooses which `libSceAmpr.sprx` a game reads, so the game runs the version you > picked. ## Prerequisites - A jailbroken ps5 with an ELF loader listening on port 9021. - **NanoDNS** running, the first time — after that the payload keeps its own offline copy of the APR Emu builds and no longer needs the internet. - **ShadowMountPlus** for games installed as image files. Both branches work: - **1.7alpha7 or newer** — the payload uses ShadowMountPlus's own emulator slot. Nothing is mounted over your games. - **1.6beta16 and older** — the payload mounts the override itself, as it always has. ## Upgrading from an earlier version > [!WARNING] > **Delete everything inside `/data/apr-emu-updater/` before using this > release.** State from earlier versions is laid out differently and will > conflict. This clears your staged versions and the offline copy; both are > rebuilt from scratch. For Shadowmount Alpha, update `update_emulators` to `1` in `/data/shadowmount/config.ini`. ShadowMountPlus will ignore the override. You can edit that file from the payload's own **ShadowMountPlus config** tab. ## How to use it **Send `apr_emu_updater_v2.0.6.elf` to your ps5**, port 9021, with whatever you normally use to send payloads. The ps5 shows: ```text APR Emu Updater listening on http://192.168.1.20:6971/ ``` The first time it also installs an **APR Emu Updater** tile, so you can reach the page later without typing an address. Open the page from the tile, or type that address into a phone or computer on the same network. ### Setting a version for a game ShadowMountPlus 1.7 mounts a game's image only while the game is running, so the payload cannot see what APR Emu a game carries until it has run once. 1. **Launch the game once, then close it.** The payload reads and remembers the APR Emu it carries while the image is mounted. 2. **Open the page.** The game now shows its version and offers actions. Games that have never been launched are listed but offer nothing yet. 3. **Choose a version** — **Update** for the newest, or **Select version** for a specific one, including debug builds. The column shows the version you picked. 4. **Launch the game again.** The override is applied as the game starts, and a notification confirms which build is live. Repeat step 1 for each game you want to manage. ### One version for every game If you would rather not choose per game, switch **Override mode** to **Global**. The game list is replaced by a single version picker, and ShadowMountPlus applies that one build to every game that uses APR Emu. ## Good to know - **Per game mode needs the payload loaded.** The override is set up as each game starts, so send the payload after every reboot, or let an autoloader do it. You do not need to open the tile — only to have the payload running. - **Global mode does not.** That version is written to ShadowMountPlus's own folder and stays there, so it survives reboots with no payload loaded. - **Games installed as folders are changed on disk** and stay changed either way. - **It works offline.** The APR Emu builds are copied to your console the first time the payload runs with a connection. After that, versions and installs work with no internet at all. Use **Fetch latest builds** on the Offline builds tab when you want new ones. - **Nothing is used unless it is verified.** Every build is checked against the size and SHA-256 the version list declares — when it is downloaded, and again every time it is read from the offline copy. - **The page follows your language.** Spanish, Japanese, French, German and Arabic are translated, with English for everything else. Corrections from native speakers are welcome. ## If something looks wrong | What you see | What it means | | --- | --- | | The tile opens an empty browser page | The payload is not loaded. Send it again, then tap the tile | | A game is listed with no buttons | It has not been launched yet. Start it once, close it, and it will fill in | | "did not take the APR Emu override" | The game started before the override was ready. Close it and start it again | | A game says APR Emu is missing | That game has no `libSceAmpr.sprx` to replace, so there is nothing to change | | A game is listed as unsupported | Its image is a raw `.ffpfs`, which cannot be overridden | | No versions listed, first run | The ps5 could not reach the internet. Check NanoDNS, then use **Fetch latest builds** | | Anything else | Press **Logs** on the page. It shows what the payload did, step by step | ## Where the versions come from The APR Emu builds are in this repository, under `apr-emu/`, and the payload reads the list from: ```text https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tsuramatsu1/apr-emu-updater/main/apr-emu/builds.json ``` They are copied to `/data/apr-emu-updater/apr-emu/` on your console and read from there afterwards. Nothing else is contacted, and nothing is downloaded from anywhere else.

repos.name: PS5-Game-Compressor
repos.description: Standalone PS5 payload for compressing, unpacking, validating, and repairing ShadowMountPlus-mounted games
repos.readme:
# PS5 Game Compressor

Standalone PS5 payload for compressing, unpacking, validating, repairing, and
moving ShadowMountPlus-mounted games from a simple web UI.

Game Compressor is made for the day-to-day workflow after your games are already
mounted through ShadowMountPlus: pick a title, choose an action, and let the PS5
do the work. The app keeps long operations running on the console even if the
browser window is closed.

## Rest mode and interrupted jobs

During ordinary copying, compression, unpacking, scanning, and validation,
Game Compressor allows automatic rest mode. If the PS5 preserves the payload
process, the worker continues after wake and the web UI refreshes its progress
and history when reopened. During source deletion, destructive stream
compression, block repair, and mount/configuration changes, Game Compressor
renews the console's automatic rest timer until the critical phase ends.

The power timer cannot prevent someone from choosing rest mode manually.
Avoid manual rest while an operation is changing existing game data. If the
payload stops during rest or restarts afterward, unfinished jobs are recorded
as interrupted in history. Queued jobs are cancelled, and running jobs are
marked failed; neither is restarted automatically. Inspect the source and
output paths before retrying, especially after destructive compression or
deletion.

## Main Features

- Compress mounted game folders or images into FF-PFSC output.
- Choose PFS or exFAT output when compressing.
- Automatically build APR Emu `ampr_emu.index` before compressing APR titles.
- Manually run `Build AMPR Index` on a folder when you only want to refresh the
  APR index.
- Validate compressed games and repair detected PFSC block issues when possible.
- Uncompress compressed games back to folder/app form.
- Move supported titles between internal storage and USB storage.
- Track progress, speed, estimated remaining time, and operation history.
- Keep operations running on the PS5 even if the browser tab closes.
- Install or refresh a PS5 home-screen launcher tile:

```text
Game Compressor / PSGC50001 -> http://127.0.0.1:5910/
```

The PS5 home-screen tile opens the Game Compressor web UI in the browser. It is
not the compression worker itself. Compression, validation, repair, move, and
uncompress jobs continue on the PS5 if you close the browser window or reopen
the tile later.

## APR Emu Support

APR Emu titles need an `ampr_emu.index` file and the correct ShadowMountPlus
read-only image settings when they are run from internal SSD. Game Compressor
handles those details for the common workflows:

- To compress a folder-format APR Emu game from USB and run it from internal
  SSD, plug in the USB drive, select the title, and choose `Compress`. Game
  Compressor builds `ampr_emu.index` using the same workflow as
  `build_ampr_index.py`, writes the ShadowMountPlus read-only and sector-size
  settings, creates the `.ffpfsc` image, mounts it, and validates the mounted
  image byte-for-byte against the original.
- If the compressed game stutters and you still want it on internal SSD, open
  the secondary action menu, choose `Uncompress`, then select `exFAT`. The
  ShadowMountPlus settings and `ampr_emu.index` are already in place, so Game
  Compressor leaves them unchanged and creates an uncompressed exFAT image.
- If you already know the game should stay uncompressed, open the secondary
  action menu, choose `Make Image`, then select `exFAT` and `Internal SSD`.
  Game Compressor detects the APR Emu title, builds or refreshes
  `ampr_emu.index`, applies the read-only ShadowMountPlus settings, and creates
  the uncompressed image.
- If you already have an exFAT image and `ampr_emu.index` exists, use `Set Read
  Only` from the secondary action menu to apply the ShadowMountPlus read-only
  settings for that image.

The only unsupported automatic case is an existing exFAT image with no
`ampr_emu.index`. For that case, run the game once from external USB without
read-only settings so APR Emu can create its index, confirm the game starts,
then copy it to internal SSD and use `Set Read Only`.

Non-APR titles keep the normal compression path. When APR indexing is performed,
the selected game screen and operation history show `APR indexed`.

The in-app `APR-EMU Version` picker uses Pippo's public APR-EMU manifest and
binary mirror:

```text
https://pippo26442999.github.io/.exFAT/ampr-emu-drakmor/manifest.json
```

The manifest and hosted files are provided by Pippo (`pippo26442999`). Manifest
entries are downloaded by the browser, uploaded to Game Compressor, cached under
`/data/GameCompressor/ampr-emu`, and then applied to the selected title or
image. Custom `.sprx`/`.prx` files can also be uploaded manually from a desktop
browser. The upstream APR Emu project source is
[drakmor/ampr_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/ampr_emu).

## Requirements

- A PS5 homebrew environment capable of running payload ELFs.
- [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus) latest version,
  installed and managing mounted titles.
- [KStuff Lite](https://github.com/EchoStretch/kstuff-lite/releases/tag/v1.07)
  1.07 Beta or later.
- [Payload Manager](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager) or another
  method to launch `game-compressor.elf`.

This project assumes you already understand the risks of running PS5 homebrew
payloads. Keep backups of important data and test with non-critical titles
first.

## Build

For firmware 13.60, use [ps5-payload-sdk v0.43](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk/releases/tag/v0.43)
or newer. Its CRT contains the 13.60 kernel initialization case. Earlier
Game Compressor builds can fail before `main()` and create no application log.
The build checks the SDK CRT for that case and refuses an unsupported SDK.

On Linux or WSL, install `make`, Python 3, Clang 18, and LLD 18. Set
`PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK` to the extracted SDK path, then run `make`:

```sh
export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk
make
```

The needed zlib 1.3.1 sources are included under `third_party/zlib` and are
built for PS5 along with the payload. No external zlib path is required.

The build output is:

```text
game-compressor.elf
```

The 13.60 build has been checked for successful compilation and ELF format.
A locally built payload was also launched successfully on a PS5 running
firmware 13.60.

GitHub Actions builds the ELF on pushes and pull requests. Pushing a `v*` tag
also creates or updates a GitHub Release containing `game-compressor.elf` and
`SHA256SUMS`. The workflow downloads the pinned SDK v0.43 release, verifies its
SHA-256 checksum, and checks that its CRT contains the firmware 13.60 case.

Generated build outputs are intentionally ignored by git:

```text
build/
gen/
game-compressor.elf
```

## Deploy

Copy the built ELF to your PS5 payload folder. A typical Payload Manager path is:

```text
/data/pldmgr/payloads/game-compressor/game-compressor.elf
```

This repo also includes Payload Manager metadata in:

```text
payload-manager/game-compressor.elf.json
```

If you rebuild the ELF, update that JSON checksum before publishing or
redistributing it.

## How To Use

1. Make sure ShadowMountPlus has mounted one or more games.
2. Launch `game-compressor.elf` from Payload Manager or your payload loader.
3. Open the web UI:

```text
http://<PS5_IP>:5910/
```

4. Pick a game from the left sidebar.
5. Use the primary action:
   - Folder/image titles show `Compress`.
   - Compressed titles show `Validate and Repair`.
6. For compression, choose either `PFS` or `exFAT` when prompted.
7. Use the secondary action menu for supported actions such as:
   - `Build AMPR Index`
   - `Uncompress`
   - `Move to USB`
   - `Move to Internal SSD`
8. Use the History button to review previous operations.

The app remembers the last game you viewed using a browser cookie, so reopening
the UI returns to that title when it is still available.

If you close the browser window during an operation, open the Game Compressor
tile again or go back to `http://<PS5_IP>:5910/` to see the current job.

## Compression Settings

When you choose `Compress`, Game Compressor asks for the output format,
destination, and how to handle the original source.

### Format

`Compress` always produces a `.ffpfsc` file, which is a compressed PFS container.
The format choice controls the nested image stored inside that compressed
container:

- `exFAT` is the default and recommended nested image format. It stores an exFAT
  image inside the `.ffpfsc` output and is the preferred option for most games,
  especially APR Emu workflows.
- `PFS Experimental` stores a PFS image inside the `.ffpfsc` output. Use it only
  when you specifically want to test the PFS nested-image path.

### Destination

- `Compress in place` writes the compressed `.ffpfsc` container next to the
  currently selected game.
- `Internal SSD` writes the compressed output under `/data/homebrew`. This is
  only shown when the selected game is not already on internal storage.
- `External Storage` writes the compressed output to a selected USB/external
  target. If the game is already on external storage, Game Compressor may show a
  `Compress to...` picker so you can choose internal SSD or another USB target.

### Original Handling

- `Keep original` leaves the source folder or image untouched. This is the
  safest choice and requires enough free space for the compressed output.
- `Delete after verified` writes and validates the compressed output first, then
  removes the original source. This is the default for in-place compression. It
  still needs full-size temporary free space because the original is kept until
  verification succeeds.
- `Destructive` deletes source data while writing the compressed output. It
  requires at least 1 GB of free space, cannot be cancelled after the unsafe
  phase begins, and is only available for same-storage folder compression. It is
  not available when compressing to another drive or when using `Make Image`.

When compressing to internal SSD or external storage, Game Compressor keeps the
original by default. If you choose to remove the original, it uses the safer
`Delete after verified` behavior.

## Game Discovery

Mounted games are shown automatically. Game Compressor also scans known game
storage folders, including:

```text
/data/homebrew
/data/etaHEN/games
/mnt/ext0
/mnt/ext0/homebrew
/mnt/ext0/etaHEN/games
/mnt/ext1
/mnt/ext1/homebrew
/mnt/ext1/etaHEN/games
/mnt/usb0 through /mnt/usb7
/mnt/usb0/homebrew through /mnt/usb7/homebrew
/mnt/usb0/etaHEN/games through /mnt/usb7/etaHEN/games
```

## When You Are Done

Game Compressor should only be launched when you need to compress, validate,
repair, move, or unpack games. After your games are compressed and you no longer
need the web UI, it is preferred that Game Compressor is no longer running.

Use the terminate button in the top bar when you are done. Game Compressor
removes its home-screen tile, stops the payload, and leaves a final screen
telling you to exit the browser window.

## Notes

- Launcher installation is nonfatal. If it fails, the web UI can still be used
  directly from `http://<PS5_IP>:5910/`.
- Payload operations are owned by the PS5-side worker, not the browser tab.
- Compression and repair workflows can take a long time on large titles.

## Credits

Created by Juma Sayeh.

Tested by Osama Abualia.

Thanks to Pippo (`pippo26442999`) for maintaining the public APR-EMU manifest
and binary mirror used by the in-app APR-EMU version picker.

Built on and inspired by work from:

- [PSBrew/MkPFS](https://github.com/PSBrew/MkPFS)
- Drakmor's [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus),
  [APR Emu](https://github.com/drakmor/ampr_emu), and `build_ampr_index.py`
  work, which Game Compressor builds on for mounted-title support and PS5-side
  `ampr_emu.index` generation.

Made with love in Palestine.

## Disclaimer

This is homebrew software for experimental PS5 workflows. Use it at your own
risk. The project is not affiliated with Sony, PlayStation, or any game
publisher.

# ps5-exfat2ampr

![Testé et fonctionnel sur PlayStation 5](docs/tested-on-ps5.svg)

✅ **Testé et fonctionnel sur PlayStation 5** par l'auteur, V-10 (firmware 12.xx & 13.xx, kstuff, ShadowMountPlus 1.7).

Payload PS5 (jailbreak + chargeur d'ELF) qui convertit **sur la console** un jeu
en pack **AMPR LZ4** (format d'ampr_emu / Lazy_AMPR) et le dépose dans le dossier
`homebrew` du support de votre choix : SSD interne, SSD M.2 étendu ou USB. Aucun PC
dans la boucle : on envoie l'ELF, on ouvre la page web depuis un téléphone, on
choisit le jeu et la destination, on lance. La conversion peut être mise en pause,
survit à un arrêt de la console et reprend à l'octet près.

```
/mnt/usb0/homebrew/PPSA01234      (dump dossier sur clé exFAT)
/mnt/shadowmnt/PPSA01234_xxxx     (image .exfat montée par ShadowMountPlus)
        │
        ▼  exfat2ampr.elf (sur la PS5)
        │   scan → profil → ampr_emu.index → LZ4 par blocs 64 KiB, dédoublonnés → ampr_assets-NNN.pak
        │   + ampr_assets.index (+ .crc, .runtime) + fichiers loose + fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx
        │   → vérification de chaque bloc
        ▼
/data/homebrew/PPSA01234     ou   /mnt/ext0/homebrew/PPSA01234   ou   /mnt/usb0/homebrew/PPSA01234
```

## Utilisation

1. Envoyer `exfat2ampr.elf` à la console (port 9021 : etaHEN, elfldr, websrv…).
   Une notification affiche l'adresse, par exemple `http://192.168.1.20:6972/`.
2. Ouvrir cette adresse depuis un téléphone ou un PC du même réseau. L'interface
   existe en français, anglais, espagnol, italien, russe et arabe.
3. **Source** : dump dossier sur clé USB (`homebrew/<jeu>`), image montée, ou chemin
   manuel. Une image `.exfat` non montée propose un bouton « Monter via
   ShadowMountPlus » (inscription dans `manual.lst`).
4. **Destination** : supports détectés automatiquement avec l'espace libre. Les
   supports non inscriptibles sont grisés ; la conversion refuse de démarrer si
   l'espace est manifestement insuffisant.
5. **Options** : niveau LZ4 (9 HC par défaut), threads, vérification (recommandée),
   dédoublonnage, nettoyage des restes de dump, remplacement, suppression de la source.
6. **Convertir** ajoute à la file d'attente ; plusieurs jeux s'enchaînent seuls.
7. **Progression** : barre, octets traités, débit, temps écoulé et restant, journal.
   **Pause** arrête proprement ; **Annuler** supprime le dossier en cours.
8. **Conversions interrompues** : tout dossier laissé en pause, ou interrompu par un
   arrêt, un mode repos ou un disque plein, apparaît ici avec **Reprendre** ou
   **Abandonner**.
9. **Profils par jeu** : `<TITLE_ID>.toml` déposés dans `USB:\homebrew\profiles\`
   (importés au démarrage) ou collés dans la page. Un sous-ensemble du format
   d'ampr_pack est compris : `[[rule]]` avec `action` (`compress`, `store`, `loose`),
   `include`, `exclude`, et `[pack] compression_level`. La dernière règle gagne. Les
   profils de Lazy_AMPR (`toml_profiles/`) se chargent tels quels.

Mode automatique : `exfat2ampr.elf --auto` met en file tout jeu trouvé dans
`/mnt/usb*/homebrew/` qui n'est pas encore dans `/data/homebrew`.

## Application sur l'écran d'accueil (PPSA99272)

La même chose à la manette, sans téléphone ni PC. Prérequis : kstuff à jour, un
chargeur d'ELF sur le port 9021 (elfldr, ou etaHEN : depuis la 1.7beta5,
ShadowMountPlus conseille de ne plus utiliser etaHEN) et ShadowMountPlus 1.7 ou plus
récent.

1. Copier `PPSA99272.ffpkg` dans `homebrew\` à la racine d'une clé USB exFAT, ou par
   FTP (serveur d'etaHEN, ou payload FTP sans etaHEN) dans `/data/homebrew/` (l'app
   reste alors disponible sans clé). En secours :
   le contenu de `PPSA99272-folder.zip` dans `/data/homebrew/PPSA99272/`.
2. ShadowMountPlus détecte l'image (une trentaine de secondes) et ajoute
   **exFAT2AMPR** à l'écran d'accueil.
3. Au lancement, l'app envoie elle-même son moteur au chargeur d'ELF (port 9021) :
   plus besoin d'envoyer `exfat2ampr.elf` à la main. Si un ancien moteur a été lancé
   à la main depuis le dernier démarrage, redémarrer la console d'abord.

Commandes : ↑↓ choisir, □ cocher plusieurs jeux, ✕ continuer (options →
destination → vérification → lancement), L1/R1 onglets (Progression, Interrompues,
Réglages), △ pause/reprise, ◯ retour. La conversion continue app fermée ou en jeu.
Une conversion en erreur n'est jamais bloquée : ✕ la relance (ou la reprend depuis
son point de reprise), □ l'efface. Chaque erreur est expliquée dans la langue choisie,
avec ce qu'il faut faire.

Version : affichée à côté du titre (par exemple `v1.137`), sur l'écran de démarrage, dans
Réglages et sur la page web. Le nombre augmente à chaque nouvelle version ; c'est aussi la
version que la console indique pour l'app (`01.000.137`). Si Réglages affiche un moteur
d'une autre version (en orange), redémarrer la console puis relancer l'app.

Jeux trouvés : dossiers `homebrew` de la console, des disques USB et du SSD M.2, dossiers
`etaHEN/games`, racine des disques (et un niveau de sous-dossier, par exemple
`<disque>/<nom de la release>/<jeu>`), plus tout ce que gère ShadowMountPlus. Chaque jeu indique
où il se trouve : stockage interne, USB n ou SSD M.2. Son image vient du jeu lui-même, de l'image
montée, de ShadowMountPlus ou de la copie que la console garde de chaque titre installé
(`/user/appmeta`) ; à défaut, une vignette est dessinée à partir du titre.

Langues de l'app : français, anglais, espagnol, italien, russe, portugais (Brésil),
chinois simplifié, thaï et vietnamien. Celle de la console est choisie au premier
lancement, puis Réglages → Langue. Les titres de jeux en chinois, japonais ou coréen
s'affichent aussi (caractères courants : GB2312, Big5 niveau 1, kana, kanji niveau 1,
hangul KS X 1001).

Images `.exfat` / `.ffpkg` gérées par ShadowMountPlus : SMP ne monte aucune image
tant qu'un jeu ou une application est ouvert, exFAT2AMPR compris (réponse 409
`EBUSY`, raison `game_active`). Une conversion d'image lancée depuis l'app attend
donc, sans erreur (« En attente de ShadowMountPlus », nouvel essai toutes les 5 à
20 s), et démarre seule dès que l'application est fermée : △ la ferme depuis
l'onglet Progression. Avec `persistent_image_mounts=1`, une image déjà montée est lue
directement, sans rien demander à SMP. Si le fakelib du jeu est « Désactivé » dans
SMP, il est réglé sur « Émulateurs » après la conversion : c'est le plus petit mode
qui charge encore `libSceAmpr.sprx` (sinon le jeu converti ne démarrerait pas).

Finitions : l'image de fond du jeu sélectionné (`sce_sys/pic0.png`, sinon sa jaquette
floutée) derrière des panneaux de verre fumé, animations (sélection qui glisse,
écrans qui coulissent, jaquettes en fondu, barre de progression vivante) et sons de
navigation synthétisés. **Réglages → Sons de navigation / Animations** les coupent
(les animations coupées soulagent le processeur si besoin).

Mises à jour : fermer l'app et remplacer le fichier `.ffpkg` (mise à jour
automatique prévue).

## Pause et reprise

- Le packer écrit ses tampons (enregistrements, blocs, CRC, chaînes, table de
  dédoublonnage) en mode ajout dans `<destination>/.e2a-state/` et un `state.bin`
  atomique toutes les dix secondes, à chaque fin de fichier et à la pause.
- Les volumes `.pak` sont retronqués à la position du dernier point de reprise ;
  les fichiers loose sont copiés via un temporaire puis renommés ; la phase de
  vérification redémarre du début si elle est interrompue.
- À la reprise, la source est rescannée et comparée (nombre, tailles, dates) ;
  si elle a changé, la reprise est refusée.
- Un disque plein met la conversion en pause au lieu d'échouer : libérez de la
  place, puis reprenez.

## Compilation et validation

GitHub Actions fait deux choses à chaque push :

1. **validate** : compile une version Linux (`make host`), génère un jeu
   synthétique, lance une conversion avec pause forcée à 48 Mio, la reprend, puis
   fait vérifier le résultat par les outils Python de référence de drakmor/ampr_emu
   (`ampr_pack.py verify --root`, reconstruction byte à byte).
2. **build** : compile `exfat2ampr.elf` avec le ps5-payload-sdk et publie
   l'artefact ; un tag `vX.Y.Z` crée une release.

En local (Linux ou WSL) :

```bash
sudo apt-get install bash clang-18 lld-18 wget unzip xxd curl
wget https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk/releases/latest/download/ps5-payload-sdk.zip
sudo unzip -d /opt ps5-payload-sdk.zip
export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/opt/ps5-payload-sdk
make deps && make
PS5_HOST=192.168.1.20 make test
```

```bash
make host && python3 tests/make_game.py testgame && ./exfat2ampr-host testgame homebrew
```

## Ce que fait le packer (port C de `ampr_pack.py`)

- Un seul groupe, layout `mixed`, blocs 64 KiB, page d'E/S 64 KiB, alignement 64 o.
- Lecture en avance sur un thread, compression LZ4 (fast ≤ 4, HC 5 à 12) sur N threads.
- Un bloc reste RAW si le gain est inférieur à 64 o / 1 %, ou à 8 KiB / 12,5 % quand il
  n'économise aucune page d'E/S. `store` force RAW (fichiers déjà compressés mais à
  garder seekables).
- Dédoublonnage : blocs identiques (SHA-256 tronqué + taille) partagés, flag `SHARED`.
- Auto-loose : fichiers ≥ 64 Mio dont les premiers blocs gagnent moins de 5 %.
- Toujours loose : `eboot.bin`, `.prx/.sprx/.elf/.self`, `sce_sys/`, `sce_module/`,
  `fakelib/`, `system/`, `mods/`, `save/`, `trophy2/`, `uds/`, `_DUPLEX_/`, vidéos,
  audio compressé, `.json/.xml/.utoc/.bin/.dat`, archives.
- Formats écrits : AMPRIDX3, AMPRPAK4, AMPRDAT3, AMPRCRC1, AMPRCFG1.
- Émulateur : la copie tenue à jour par ShadowMountPlus
  (`/data/shadowmount/emus/libSceAmpr.sprx`) est préférée si elle a un en-tête PRX
  valide ; sinon la 0.4.2.1 embarquée. La page affiche laquelle est utilisée et son
  SHA-256.

## Optimisation par traces (section 7 de la page)

Port C de `ampr_pack_profile.py` (drakmor/ampr_emu) : au lieu de deviner, on mesure comment le jeu lit ses fichiers.

1. **Activer le mode trace** sur un jeu de `homebrew` (converti ou non) : l'émulateur debug
   `libSceAmpr.sprx-0.4.2.1-test-debug-pack` est placé dans `<jeu>/fakelib2`. ShadowMountPlus monte `fakelib2`
   à la place de `fakelib` et ne le remplace jamais lors de la mise à jour des émulateurs. Les autres bibliothèques
   de `fakelib` y sont recopiées. Un `fakelib2` qui n'a pas été créé par exfat2ampr (backport) n'est jamais modifié.
2. **Jouer** : démarrage, chargement d'une sauvegarde, plusieurs zones, puis quitter le jeu normalement.
   Le jeu écrit `/app0/ampr_commands.bin` (journal `AMPRCMD1`).
3. **Collecter** : le journal et son `ampr_emu.index` sont copiés dans `/data/exfat2ampr/traces/<TITLE_ID>/<n>/`.
   L'émulateur vide le journal à chaque lancement : collecter après chaque session.
4. **Générer le profil** : toutes les traces sont fusionnées. Pour chaque fichier lu, on choisit :
   - la taille de bloc (16 KiB à 1 MiB) ;
   - le layout (streaming, random ou mixed) ;
   - le drapeau hot ;
   - et la section `[runtime]` : cache décodé obtenu par simulation LRU, cache physique, workers et réserve.

   Le profil est écrit dans `/data/exfat2ampr/profiles/<TITLE_ID>.toml` et s'applique à la prochaine conversion de ce
   jeu, il faut donc **garder la source**.
5. **Désactiver le mode trace** ensuite : l'émulateur debug est plus lent.

Les règles générées utilisent `action = "keep"`. Elles ne règlent que la géométrie des fichiers déjà packés et ne
font jamais packer un fichier que la liste de sécurité garde en clair. La CI compare le résultat à
`ampr_pack_profile.py` sur un journal synthétique validé par `parse_ampr_command_log.py`.

## Plugins des jeux (pgo_stub, dlc_emu)

Le moteur embarque les modules de remplacement de drakmor : `libScePlayGo.sprx`
([pgo_stub](https://github.com/drakmor/pgo_stub) : PlayGo voit tous les morceaux installés) et
`libSceAppContent.sprx`, `libSceGameUpdate.sprx`, `libSceNpEntitlementAccess.sprx`
([dlc_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/dlc_emu) : les DLC listés dans le `dlc_emu.ini` du jeu). Versions
épinglées par le Makefile et vérifiées par SHA-256 (`tools/plugins.sha256`) ; `src/plugins.c` connaît
l'empreinte de chaque version publiée, donc sait dire si un fichier d'un jeu est à jour, ancien (remplacé,
l'ancienne copie reste en `.old`) ou inconnu (laissé tel quel).

- À chaque conversion, la destination reçoit ce dont le jeu a besoin : PlayGo quand le jeu l'importe, les
  modules DLC quand le jeu a un `dlc_emu.ini` (sans ce fichier ils cacheraient les vrais DLC : jamais ajoutés
  seuls).
- Au démarrage puis toutes les 6 heures (et quand un support est branché), chaque dossier de jeu des racines
  connues est vérifié, sauf un jeu en cours d'exécution.
- Le dossier d'émulateurs de ShadowMountPlus (`/data/shadowmount/emus`, `update_emulators=1`) reçoit les mêmes
  fichiers : les jeux montés depuis une image suivent aussi.
- App : menu du jeu › « Plugins : … » (un jeu), Réglages › Plugins des jeux (tous) ; page web : état par jeu et
  bouton « Mettre à jour les plugins » ; API : `GET /api/plugins[?path=]`, `POST /api/plugins/refresh [path=]`.

Nouveau, pas encore validé sur console.

## Limites

- Non testé sur console par l'auteur de ce dépôt : la CI valide le format avec les
  outils de référence, pas l'exécution sur PS5. Première exécution à faire sur un
  petit jeu, journal dans `/data/exfat2ampr/exfat2ampr.log`.
- Le payload ne monte pas lui-même les images : il s'appuie sur ShadowMountPlus.
- Le mode repos interrompt la conversion ; elle reprend ensuite, mais désactivez-le
  pour une conversion d'un seul trait.
- L'émulateur AMPR est en bêta ; si son format évolue (AMPRPAK5…), le packer devra
  être mis à jour.

## Crédits

- **V-10** : auteur d'exFAT2AMPR (moteur, app PS5, page web).
- **DLPSGAME** : le format LZ4 des jeux PS5.
- drakmor : l'émulateur AMPR (ampr_emu) et ShadowMountPlus.
- Yann Collet : l'algorithme de compression LZ4.

## Licence

exFAT2AMPR - Copyright (C) 2026 V-10. Logiciel libre sous GNU GPL version 3 ou ultérieure (texte complet :
`COPYING`), avec des conditions supplémentaires de l'article 7 (fichier `NOTICE`) :
- toute copie ou version modifiée garde ce copyright et le crédit « Créé par V-10 » ;
- une version modifiée se présente comme modifiée et ne se fait pas passer pour l'originale ;
- le nom « exFAT2AMPR » et son logo ne sont pas cédés : une version modifiée diffusée porte un autre nom et une
  autre icône.

Retirer le nom de l'auteur ou diffuser le programme sous un autre nom d'auteur met fin aux droits accordés par
la licence (article 8).

GPL-3.0-or-later. Formats et heuristiques d'après drakmor/ampr_emu (GPL-3.0),
LZ4 (BSD-2), ps5-payload-sdk (GPL-3.0). Polices de l'app : DejaVu Sans (licence
Bitstream Vera / DejaVu), Noto Sans Thai et Noto Sans CJK (SIL Open Font License 1.1).

latestRelease.body:
## exFAT2AMPR — convert PS5 game dumps to AMPR LZ4, right on the console

![Tested and working on PlayStation 5](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/exFAT2AMPR/exfat2ampr/main/docs/tested-on-ps5.svg)

Made by **V-10** · LZ4 format: **DLPSGAME** · AMPR emulator: drakmor/ampr_emu · free software (GPL-3.0)

✅ **Tested and working on a PlayStation 5** by the author (firmware 12.xx & 13.xx, kstuff, ShadowMountPlus 1.7).

### What it does

- Finds every game and app on the console — internal storage, USB drives, M.2 SSD, `homebrew` and
  `etaHEN/games` folders, the drives' top level, and everything ShadowMountPlus manages — and shows where
  each one is kept, with its cover.
- Converts exFAT dumps (folders or images) to AMPR LZ4 packs on the PS5 itself: checks first (free space,
  AMPR compatibility, copies already converted), verifies every block, keeps the originals.
- Runs in the background, slows down while you play, resumes after an interruption.
- **Optimize this game**: measures how a game reads its files while you play and builds a profile for its
  next conversion (faster loading, fewer stutters).
- **Speed test** of each storage, the fastest one recommended, slow ones flagged.
- **Automatic updates**: the app tells you when a new version is out and installs it (the previous package
  is kept as `.old`).
- **Game plugins kept up to date**: drakmor's PlayGo stub (pgo_stub) and DLC modules (dlc_emu) are embedded.
  Every conversion gets what the game needs, every game folder is checked at start-up and from the app (the
  game's menu, or Settings › Game plugins for all of them), older releases are replaced (the old copy stays as
  `.old`), and ShadowMountPlus' emulator folder receives the same files, so the games it mounts follow too.
- **Faster conversions, packs as good**: a fast LZ4 probe skips the slow pass on incompressible data, a CRC
  four times faster, the verification on several threads; the emulator's memory budget is checked before
  the cache settings are written (a large cache no longer ends up smaller than the standard one on a big
  game).
- **Advice on every option**: "Recommended" or "Less recommended" next to each setting, with the reason in
  one line; the defaults are the recommended values.
- Nine languages: English, French, Spanish, Italian, Russian, Portuguese, Chinese, Thai, Vietnamese; the
  web page for a PC or a phone (pairing with a 6-digit code or a QR code) adds Arabic.

### Install

Requirements: a jailbroken PS5 with kstuff, an ELF loader on port 9021 (elfldr, etaHEN…), ShadowMountPlus
1.7 or newer.

1. Copy `PPSA99272.ffpkg` into `homebrew/` at the root of an exFAT USB drive, or by FTP into `/data/homebrew/`.
   Keep a single copy of it.
2. Restart the console, start the jailbreak; ShadowMountPlus adds **exFAT2AMPR** to the home screen.
3. Open it: the app starts its engine itself. `exfat2ampr.elf` is only needed to run the engine by hand.

Tested and working on a PlayStation 5 by the author (firmware 12.xx & 13.xx, kstuff, ShadowMountPlus 1.7).
Other firmwares and setups: reports are welcome. New in this version and not yet validated on a console: the
game plugin updates.

**Presentation video**: `exfat2ampr-presentation.mp4` — English voice, French subtitles.

---

### En français

exFAT2AMPR convertit les dumps de jeux PS5 au format AMPR LZ4, directement sur la console. Créé par **V-10**,
format LZ4 : **DLPSGAME**. ✅ **Testé et fonctionnel sur PlayStation 5** par l'auteur (firmware 12.xx & 13.xx,
kstuff, ShadowMountPlus 1.7). Installation : copier `PPSA99272.ffpkg` dans `homebrew/` (clé USB exFAT) ou dans
`/data/homebrew/` par FTP, en un seul exemplaire, redémarrer, lancer le jailbreak puis l'app. Les mises à jour
suivantes s'installent depuis l'app (Réglages › Mises à jour). Les plugins pgo_stub (PlayGo) et dlc_emu (DLC)
de drakmor sont intégrés et maintenus à jour dans le dossier `fakelib` des jeux : à chaque conversion, au
démarrage, depuis le menu du jeu ou Réglages › Plugins des jeux (nouveau, pas encore validé sur console).
Conversions plus rapides à packs identiques (sonde LZ4 rapide, CRC plus rapide, vérification sur plusieurs
cœurs, budget mémoire de l'émulateur respecté), et chaque option indique « Recommandé » ou « Moins
recommandé » avec la raison. La vidéo de présentation
(`exfat2ampr-presentation.mp4`, voix anglaise, sous-titres français) est jointe à la release.

repos.readme:
# LZ4 Compression for PS5

[![Buy Me a Coffee](https://img.shields.io/badge/Buy_Me_a_Coffee-Support_this_project-FFDD00?style=for-the-badge&logo=buymeacoffee&logoColor=black)](https://buymeacoffee.com/theghostonline)

![LZ4 Compression](assets-app/pic0.png)

LZ4 compression for PS5 games, done entirely on the console. Pick a game,
choose `Compress with LZ4`, and it packs the game data into seekable LZ4 asset
packs that APR-EMU reads while the game runs, checks every file, and installs
the pack-capable APR-EMU runtime (adding it when the game ships none). The game
never has to leave the console.

It also does everything around that: `.ffpfsc` compression, exFAT/PFS images,
validate and repair, APR-EMU versions, copy and move, and a history of every
job.

Unofficial, and not affiliated with any of the projects it builds on. See
[Credits and license](#credits-and-license).

## The app

- **The PS5 app** (`LZ4 Compression`, title `PPSA99420`): a native app, no
  browser. Your library runs left to right like the home screen, every game
  opens its own page, and every action opens as a full page. D-pad and stick
  navigation with controller vibration, and Circle goes back.
- **The engine** (`lz4-compression.elf`): the payload that does the work. It
  serves the app and the web page on port `5920` and keeps its settings,
  caches and logs in `/data/LZ4Compression`. The app starts it through
  Payload Manager when it isn't running.
- **The web page** at `http://<PS5 IP>:5920` has the same features from a PC
  or phone, and it's where you upload TOML profiles from another device.
- It doesn't share a tile, port or settings folder with Game Compressor, so
  both can be installed.

## Install

1. Download `lz4-compression.elf` and `LZ4-Compression-PPSA99420.zip` from
   the [latest release](https://github.com/theghostonline/PS5-LZ4-Compression/releases/latest).
2. Add `lz4-compression.elf` to Payload Manager, so it sits at
   `/data/pldmgr/payloads/lz4-compression/lz4-compression.elf`. The app starts
   it from there.
3. Unzip the app and copy the `PPSA99420` folder to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99420`
   over FTP. ShadowMount+ adds the `LZ4 Compression` tile. It doesn't scan
   while a game is running, so close any game if the tile doesn't show up.
4. Open the tile. If the engine isn't running, the app starts it.

You can also skip the app: load the ELF and open `http://<PS5 IP>:5920` in
any browser.

## LZ4 asset packs

APR-EMU (drakmor's [ampr_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/ampr_emu)) can read
game data from seekable LZ4 asset packs while the game runs. LZ4 Compression
builds those packs for you:

1. Builds `ampr_emu.index` for the complete game.
2. Picks what to pack. The automatic profile scans the game: game data is
   packed, while executables, PRX/SPRX, `sce_sys`, `sce_module`, `fakelib`,
   saves, configs and already-compressed media stay loose. Large files that
   LZ4 can't shrink are sampled and left loose automatically.
3. Compresses every block with LZ4 at the level you pick (1 to 12) on all CPU cores.
4. Writes `ampr_assets.index`, its `.crc` and `.runtime` sidecars and the
   `ampr_assets-*.pak` volumes (AMPRPAK4 / AMPRDAT3, the same format
   `ampr_pack.py` writes).
5. Checks every packed file byte for byte against the original before
   anything is deleted.
6. Installs the pack-capable APR-EMU runtime (0.4.2.1 PackedStdio) into
   `fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx`.

### How to use it

LZ4 is the main action for every game that uses AMPR, which is most PS5
games, whether or not the dump ships APR-EMU. The app checks the game's
`eboot.bin` and `sce_module` for the `libSceAmpr` import. When the game has no
`fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx`, packing adds the pack-capable APR-EMU runtime
there, and ShadowMount+ loads it in place of the system module when the game
starts. A game that never imports AMPR can't load APR-EMU, so it gets
`.ffpfsc` compression instead. Folder games work directly; `.exfat`, `.ffpfs`
and `.ffpfsc` images are mounted through ShadowMount+ for the job (close any
running game first, ShadowMount+ won't mount while one is open).

Open the game from the library: `Compress with LZ4` is its main button.
`.ffpfsc` Compress is under Options.

- **Compression level:** the same 1 to 12 scale as Lazy_AMPR. 1 to 4 use
  LZ4's fast mode, 5 to 12 use LZ4 HC. 9 is the default, 12 is the smallest
  and slowest.
- **Packing profile:** `Automatic` picks the best profile on its own. The
  app ships the tested community profiles from [`profiles/`](profiles/)
  (ASTRO BOT, EA Sports UFC 6, and the Insomniac and Unity engine profiles)
  and matches them by Title ID, by name, or by the game's file layout, so a
  matching game already has the right TOML when you open it. The game page
  shows which one it will use. Games without a match get the scan-based
  profile, and `Scan only` skips the bundled one.
- `Custom or Trace Config` uses your own
  `ampr_pack` TOML, for example one generated from APR traces with
  `ampr_pack_profile.py` or a community profile for the game. Two ways to get
  one in:
  - **Import config** in the PS5 app (or Import From Console on the web page)
    lists the `.toml` files in `/data/LZ4Compression/import` and on any USB
    drive (top folder, `toml`, `tomls`, `toml_profiles`, `profiles`,
    `LZ4Compression` or `Lazy_AMPR`). Files named after the Title ID or the
    game's name show up first, the same matching Lazy_AMPR uses.
    `include_from` lists next to the TOML are copied with it.
  - Upload `profile.toml` plus any `include_from` lists it names from a PC
    or phone browser.

  Your own config always wins over the bundled one. Profiles are stored in
  `/data/LZ4Compression/lz4-profiles/<TITLE_ID>/`, and the scan-based
  profile also learns the loose rules from every bundled and uploaded
  profile.
- **Destination:** next to the game, internal SSD or external storage. The
  output is a game folder named `<name>-lz4`.
- **Original handling:**
  - `Keep original` leaves the source alone.
  - `Delete after verified` removes it after the packs and every copied file
    were checked.
  - `Pack in place` (folders only) writes the packs inside the game folder,
    verifies them, then removes only the originals that are now inside the
    packs. It needs the least free space. If anything fails before the
    removal step, the folder, its `ampr_emu.index` and its APR-EMU file are
    put back exactly as they were.

LZ4 packed games show an `LZ4 Packed` chip, and their main action becomes
`Verify LZ4 Packs`, which decodes every block and checks it against the CRC
sidecar. `Uncompress LZ4` restores the loose game, either in place or as a new
folder.

While a game is LZ4 packed, `Build AMPR Index`, `Choose APR-EMU Version` and
`Restore Original APR-EMU` are blocked: the packs are tied to that exact
`ampr_emu.index`, and only the PackedStdio runtime can read them. The original
APR-EMU file is backed up first, so `Restore Original APR-EMU` is offered
again once you uncompress that folder in place. Compress to `.ffpfsc` and Make Image still work on a
packed folder and keep its index untouched.

### How it was checked

- The C packer was compared with drakmor's `ampr_pack.py` driven by
  Lazy_AMPR's own profile generator on the same files. File records, chunk
  records, pack volumes and CRC sidecars are byte-identical at LZ4 HC 9 and
  HC 12, with the automatic profile, a custom profile (streaming, striping,
  `store`, hash and round-robin lanes, group dedupe, volume rollover,
  `include_from`) and with learned loose patterns. Only the build ID differs.
  LZ4 fast output matches the official LZ4 1.10.0 library (`ampr_pack.py`
  with python-lz4 uses LZ4 1.9.4, which compresses fast mode differently).
- `ampr_pack.py verify --root`, `inspect` and `unpack` accept the packs built
  on the PS5.
- On a PS5 running firmware 13.60, packing, verifying, unpacking and in-place
  round trips through the app gave byte-identical results, on both
  internal storage and an exFAT M.2 drive.
- Packing straight from a ShadowMountPlus-mounted `.exfat` image on the PS5
  passed `ampr_pack.py verify --root` against the original files, and
  unpacking those packs gave back every file byte for byte. `.ffpfsc` sources
  use the same code path but haven't been tested on a console yet.

Results vary by game, and a trace-based profile is more reliable than the
automatic one. Keep a backup and launch the
game before you delete its original.

## Firmware 13.60 and ShadowMountPlus 1.7

Works with the current mount stack, so `Validate`, `Validate and Repair` and
`Update APR-EMU` work on current consoles:

- **Built with ps5-payload-sdk v0.43**, whose CRT supports firmware 13.60.
- **Accepts ShadowMountPlus 1.7's layered `mount_img.lnk` format.** SMP 1.7
  writes the link to the *outer* container (`layers=2`, e.g.
  `/data/homebrew/GAME.ffpfsc`) instead of the 1.6-style nested path
  (`/mnt/shadowmnt/pfsc/<name>/GAME.exfat`). The remount verification now
  derives the expected nested directory from the actual link and accepts the
  layered form, so compressed `.ffpfsc` titles pass the mount gate again.
- **Accepts folder titles exposed as real files on `/system_ex`** (firmware
  13.60 behavior with kstuff 1.11), not only `nullfs` overlays, in the
  `system_ex` binding check used by `Update APR-EMU` and mount verification.
- **Self-healing mounts:** SMP keeps its LVD image mounts across
  restarts while LZ4 Compression clears mount links at the start of
  mount-dependent operations, which could previously leave both sides waiting
  on each other. While waiting for a remount, LZ4 Compression now asks SMP's
  local API to mount the title (`POST 127.0.0.1:10101/api/v1/games/mount`)
  after 5 s and every 15 s afterwards, so `Validate`, `Validate and Repair`,
  and compress finalize recover on their own. The nudge is a best-effort
  hint: if SMP's API is disabled the wait falls back to the previous
  scan/restart behavior.

Tested on PS5 firmware **13.60** with **kstuff-lite 1.11** and
**ShadowMountPlus 1.7beta3/1.7beta4**: a 67 GB title compressed to `.ffpfsc`
(19.5 GB) and its full hash validation (1,029,215 blocks) completed clean,
with the title mounted and launchable afterwards.

## Rest mode and interrupted jobs

During ordinary copying, compression, unpacking, scanning, and validation,
LZ4 Compression allows automatic rest mode. If the PS5 preserves the payload
process, the worker continues after wake and the web UI refreshes its progress
and history when reopened. During source deletion, destructive stream
compression, block repair, and mount/configuration changes, LZ4 Compression
renews the console's automatic rest timer until the critical phase ends.

The power timer cannot prevent someone from choosing rest mode manually.
Avoid manual rest while an operation is changing existing game data. If the
payload stops during rest or restarts afterward, unfinished jobs are recorded
as interrupted in history. Queued jobs are cancelled, and running jobs are
marked failed; neither is restarted automatically. Inspect the source and
output paths before retrying, especially after destructive compression or
deletion.

## Main Features

- Compress mounted game folders or images into FF-PFSC output.
- Choose PFS or exFAT output when compressing.
- Automatically build APR Emu `ampr_emu.index` before compressing APR titles.
- Manually run `Build AMPR Index` on a folder when you only want to refresh the
  APR index.
- Compress games into seekable LZ4 asset packs on the PS5, verify
  them, and uncompress them again (see above).
- Validate compressed games and repair detected PFSC block issues when possible.
- Uncompress compressed games back to folder/app form.
- Move supported titles between internal storage and USB storage.
- Track progress, speed, estimated remaining time, and operation history.
- Keep operations running on the PS5 even if the app or the browser tab
  closes.

## APR Emu Support

APR Emu titles need an `ampr_emu.index` file and the correct ShadowMountPlus
read-only image settings when they are run from internal SSD. LZ4 Compression
handles those details for the common workflows:

- To compress a folder-format APR Emu game from USB and run it from internal
  SSD, plug in the USB drive, select the title, and choose `Compress`. The
  app builds `ampr_emu.index` using the same workflow as
  `build_ampr_index.py`, writes the ShadowMountPlus read-only and sector-size
  settings, creates the `.ffpfsc` image, mounts it, and validates the mounted
  image byte-for-byte against the original.
- If the compressed game stutters and you still want it on internal SSD, open
  the game page and choose `Uncompress` under Options, then select `exFAT`. The
  ShadowMountPlus settings and `ampr_emu.index` are already in place, so the
  app leaves them unchanged and creates an uncompressed exFAT image.
- If you already know the game should stay uncompressed, choose `Make Image`
  under Options, then select `exFAT` and `Internal SSD`.
  LZ4 Compression detects the APR Emu title, builds or refreshes
  `ampr_emu.index`, applies the read-only ShadowMountPlus settings, and creates
  the uncompressed image.
- If you already have an exFAT image and `ampr_emu.index` exists, use `Set Read
  Only` under Options to apply the ShadowMountPlus read-only
  settings for that image.

The only unsupported automatic case is an existing exFAT image with no
`ampr_emu.index`. For that case, run the game once from external USB without
read-only settings so APR Emu can create its index, confirm the game starts,
then copy it to internal SSD and use `Set Read Only`.

Non-APR titles keep the normal compression path. When APR indexing is performed,
the selected game screen and operation history show `APR indexed`.

The in-app `APR-EMU Version` picker uses Pippo's public APR-EMU manifest and
binary mirror:

```text
https://pippo26442999.github.io/.exFAT/ampr-emu-drakmor/manifest.json
```

The manifest and hosted files are provided by Pippo (`pippo26442999`). Manifest
entries are downloaded by the browser, uploaded to LZ4 Compression, cached under
`/data/LZ4Compression/ampr-emu`, and then applied to the selected title or
image. Custom `.sprx`/`.prx` files can also be uploaded manually from a desktop
browser. The upstream APR Emu project source is
[drakmor/ampr_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/ampr_emu).

## Requirements

- A PS5 homebrew environment capable of running payload ELFs.
- [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus) latest version,
  installed and managing mounted titles.
- [KStuff Lite](https://github.com/EchoStretch/kstuff-lite/releases/tag/v1.07)
  1.07 Beta or later.
- [Payload Manager](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager) or another
  method to launch `lz4-compression.elf`.

This project assumes you already understand the risks of running PS5 homebrew
payloads. Keep backups of important data and test with non-critical titles
first.

## Build

For firmware 13.60, use [ps5-payload-sdk v0.43](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk/releases/tag/v0.43)
or newer. Its CRT contains the 13.60 kernel initialization case. Earlier
builds can fail before `main()` and create no application log.
The build checks the SDK CRT for that case and refuses an unsupported SDK.

On Linux or WSL, install `make`, Python 3, Clang 18, and LLD 18. Set
`PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK` to the extracted SDK path, then run `make`:

```sh
export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk
make
```

The needed zlib 1.3.1 sources are included under `third_party/zlib` and are
built for PS5 along with the payload. No external zlib path is required.

The build output is:

```text
lz4-compression.elf
```

The 13.60 build has been checked for successful compilation and ELF format.
A locally built payload was also launched successfully on a PS5 running
firmware 13.60.

GitHub Actions builds the ELF on pushes and pull requests. Pushing a `v*` tag
also creates or updates a GitHub Release containing `lz4-compression.elf` and
`SHA256SUMS`. The workflow downloads the pinned SDK v0.43 release, verifies its
SHA-256 checksum, and checks that its CRT contains the firmware 13.60 case.

LZ4 1.10.0 (`third_party/lz4`) and the pinned APR-EMU PackedStdio runtime
(`third_party/ampr_emu`, SHA-256 checked at build time) are included too.

The LZ4 packer also builds on a PC so it can be checked against
`ampr_pack.py`:

```sh
make -f tests/host/Makefile
build/host/ampr_pack_cli pack <game folder> <output folder> --embedded-runtime
python ampr_pack.py verify --index <output folder>/ampr_assets.index --root <game folder>
```

`tests/ps5/Makefile` builds `lz4-selftest.elf`, which packs, verifies,
unpacks and round-trips `/data/lz4test/game` on the console and writes
`/data/lz4test/selftest.log`.

`tests/ui/run.sh` checks the web UI on a PC: it starts a stub of the payload
API and drives the page in Playwright's WebKit (library, game pages, LZ4 and
compress pages, back navigation, splash and done screens, phone width). It
needs Pillow and Playwright (`pip install pillow playwright` and
`playwright install webkit`).

Generated build outputs are intentionally ignored by git:

```text
build/
gen/
lz4-compression.elf
```

## The PS5 app

`app/lz4-compression` is the console app (title `PPSA99420`): the library,
game pages and action pages with D-pad and stick navigation, controller
vibration and no browser. It talks to the engine (`lz4-compression.elf`) on
`127.0.0.1:5920` and starts it through Payload Manager when it isn't running.
The web page on port 5920 stays available from a PC or phone, for example to
upload LZ4 profiles.

It is built with [PS5 React](https://github.com/half144/ps5-react) on macOS
(Apple Silicon):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/half144/ps5-react.git && cd ps5-react
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt && npm ci
brew install cmake sdl2 llvm@18 curl libarchive
PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" npm run dev -- --app-dir ../PS5-LZ4-Compression/app/lz4-compression    # desktop preview
PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" npm run build -- --app-dir ../PS5-LZ4-Compression/app/lz4-compression  # dist/PPSA99420
```

Keep LLVM 18 out of `PATH` (the build finds it on its own); the host tools
need Apple's clang. Copy `dist/PPSA99420` to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99420` and
ShadowMount+ adds the tile.

## Deploy

Copy the built ELF to your PS5 payload folder. A typical Payload Manager path is:

```text
/data/pldmgr/payloads/lz4-compression/lz4-compression.elf
```

This repo also includes Payload Manager metadata in:

```text
payload-manager/lz4-compression.elf.json
```

Fill in its `checksum` with the SHA-256 of the ELF you publish (each build
has its own linker build ID, so every build has a different hash; release
builds list theirs in the release's `SHA256SUMS`).

## How To Use

1. Make sure ShadowMountPlus has mounted one or more games.
2. Open the `LZ4 Compression` tile, or load `lz4-compression.elf` and open
   `http://<PS5_IP>:5920/` in a browser.
3. Move along the library row and open a game.
4. Use the main button on the game page:
   - Games that use AMPR show `Compress with LZ4`.
   - Other folder and image games show `Compress` (`.ffpfsc`).
   - Compressed games show `Validate and Repair`.
   - LZ4 packed games show `Verify LZ4 Packs`.
5. Everything else is on the same page under Options, grouped as Compress,
   Check, Restore, APR-EMU, Copy and move, and Delete.
6. Use the History button in the top bar to review previous operations. The
   home screen also shows the most recent ones.

Jobs run in the engine, so they keep going if you close the app or the
browser. Open either again to see the current job. When you're done, use the
power button in the top bar to stop the engine before you play.

## Compression Settings

When you choose `Compress`, LZ4 Compression asks for the output format,
destination, and how to handle the original source.

### Format

`Compress` always produces a `.ffpfsc` file, which is a compressed PFS container.
The format choice controls the nested image stored inside that compressed
container:

- `exFAT` is the default and recommended nested image format. It stores an exFAT
  image inside the `.ffpfsc` output and is the preferred option for most games,
  especially APR Emu workflows.
- `PFS Experimental` stores a PFS image inside the `.ffpfsc` output. Use it only
  when you specifically want to test the PFS nested-image path.

### Destination

- `Compress in place` writes the compressed `.ffpfsc` container next to the
  currently selected game.
- `Internal SSD` writes the compressed output under `/data/homebrew`. This is
  only shown when the selected game is not already on internal storage.
- `External Storage` writes the compressed output to a selected USB/external
  target. If the game is already on external storage, LZ4 Compression may show a
  `Compress to...` picker so you can choose internal SSD or another USB target.

### Original Handling

- `Keep original` leaves the source folder or image untouched. This is the
  safest choice and requires enough free space for the compressed output.
- `Delete after verified` writes and validates the compressed output first, then
  removes the original source. This is the default for in-place compression. It
  still needs full-size temporary free space because the original is kept until
  verification succeeds.
- `Destructive` deletes source data while writing the compressed output. It
  requires at least 1 GB of free space, cannot be cancelled after the unsafe
  phase begins, and is only available for same-storage folder compression. It is
  not available when compressing to another drive or when using `Make Image`.

When compressing to internal SSD or external storage, LZ4 Compression keeps the
original by default. If you choose to remove the original, it uses the safer
`Delete after verified` behavior.

## Game Discovery

The library only lists games. Apps that ShadowMount+ mounts next to them
(homebrew, media apps) are left out: anything under 2 GB once its size is
known counts as an app.

Mounted games are shown automatically. LZ4 Compression also scans known game
storage folders, including:

```text
/data/homebrew
/data/etaHEN/games
/mnt/ext0
/mnt/ext0/homebrew
/mnt/ext0/etaHEN/games
/mnt/ext1
/mnt/ext1/homebrew
/mnt/ext1/etaHEN/games
/mnt/usb0 through /mnt/usb7
/mnt/usb0/homebrew through /mnt/usb7/homebrew
/mnt/usb0/etaHEN/games through /mnt/usb7/etaHEN/games
```

## When You Are Done

Only run LZ4 Compression while you need to compress, validate, repair, move or
unpack games. Once you're done, close it so it doesn't take anything away from
your games.

In the app, use the power button in the top bar and pick `Stop engine and
close`. The engine stops and the app closes, and the tile stays on the home
screen for next time. On the web page the power button stops the engine and
shows a closing screen.

## Notes

- Payload operations are owned by the PS5-side engine, not the app or the
  browser tab.
- Compression and repair workflows can take a long time on large titles.

## Support

LZ4 Compression was built and tested on a real console, one game, pack and
firmware quirk at a time. Donations here go to this project, not to the
projects it builds on (see the credits below). If it saved you space on your
PS5, a coffee helps cover the cost of building it and keeps the updates coming.

<a href="https://buymeacoffee.com/theghostonline"><img src="https://cdn.buymeacoffee.com/buttons/v2/default-yellow.png" alt="Buy Me a Coffee" height="50"></a>

Not able to donate? A star on the repository and a bug report with the game,
title ID and firmware help just as much.

## Credits and license

LZ4 Compression is built on [PS5 Game Compressor](https://github.com/juma-sayeh/PS5-Game-Compressor)
by Juma Sayeh, with firmware 13.60 and ShadowMountPlus 1.7 support by gcoding97
and Krenar, and its LZ4 side follows [Lazy_AMPR](https://github.com/Nazky/Lazy_AMPR)
by Nazky, Deckerr97, Pippo, Drakmor and williamtcastro. Packed games are read
by Drakmor's [ampr_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/ampr_emu). Third-party
components and their licenses are listed in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`; original
copyright notices are kept in the source files.

## Disclaimer

This is homebrew software for experimental PS5 workflows. Use it at your own
risk. The project is not affiliated with Sony, PlayStation, or any game
publisher. To be used with own game dumps.

# LZ4 Compression 1.4.2

Everything from 1.4.0 and 1.4.1 is included: bundled LZ4 profiles picked

while the app is open, and the `.ffpfsc` uncompress fix.

## Install

1. Add `lz4-compression.elf` to Payload Manager, so it sits at
   `/data/pldmgr/payloads/lz4-compression/lz4-compression.elf`.
2. Unzip `LZ4-Compression-PPSA99420.zip` and copy the `PPSA99420` folder to
   `/data/homebrew/PPSA99420` over FTP (replace the old one). ShadowMount+
   adds the `LZ4 Compression` tile (close any running game if it doesn't show
   up).
3. Open the tile.

Unofficial, and not affiliated with the projects it builds on. If it saved you
space, you can support the cost of building it:

repos.name: PS5-LZ4-Game-Compressor
repos.description: LZ4 game compression for PS5 homebrew — beta.1
repos.readme: # LZ4 Game Compressor **Beta 7 — On-console PS5 game compression** LZ4 Game Compressor lets you compress your PS5 games directly on your console, helping reduce the space they occupy without having to transfer them to a PC or create a separate, fully extracted copy. It converts supported PS5 game sources into AMPR LZ4 asset packs, using ShadowMountPlus to mount game images when needed. Everything is managed through a browser-based interface that you can open on your PS5 or another device connected to the same local network. ## Supported sources **This app can only convert mountable PS5 game images and extracted PS5 game folder dumps.** Images must be mountable by ShadowMountPlus. A folder dump must contain the game's `eboot.bin`, `sce_sys/param.json`, and game files. Images are read through their mounted files; the compressor does not extract the image format itself. Folder dumps are loaded through a read-only view. Already converted AMPR folders are excluded from the source library. ## Getting started ### What you'll need Before starting, make sure you have: - A homebrew-enabled PS5 - Payload Manager - ShadowMountPlus - A mountable game image supported by ShadowMountPlus, or an extracted PS5 game folder dump - Enough available storage for the converted game Keep ShadowMountPlus installed for image mounting and library refresh. Folder dumps do not need an image mount. ### Launching the compressor 1. Load `LZ4-Game-Compressor.elf` using Payload Manager. 2. Open the compressor interface in your browser at: `http://:5911/` Replace `` with your console's local IP address. 3. Your game library should appear in the interface, ready for you to select a game. The same ELF installs or refreshes the app icon and **Media shortcut** on your PS5, so no separate shortcut installer is needed. You can also access the interface using that shortcut. Keep in mind that the shortcut only opens the interface; the compressor payload must already be running. ## Compressing a game The conversion process is designed to be straightforward, with most settings handled automatically. ### 1. Select your game Find the game you want to compress in your library. Each entry is labeled **Image** or **Folder Dump** and shows its drive and source path. Make sure no game is currently running. For an image, select **Mount game**. A folder dump loads automatically; the disabled button then reads **Folder Dump Loaded**. ### 2. Choose where to save it Select the internal SSD, an available M.2 expansion SSD, or a connected USB storage device as your conversion destination. An M.2 drive must already be recognized and mounted by the PS5. Custom folders such as `/mnt/ext1/homebrew` can be selected under **Destination folders**. You can customize the exact folder locations by expanding **Destination folders**. The compressor automatically checks whether your selected drives have enough free space before allowing the conversion to start. ### 3. Decide what happens to the original You can keep the original game, delete it after conversion, move it somewhere else, or exchange its location with the compressed version. If you're trying the compressor for the first time, **Keep both** is the safest choice. This lets you test the compressed game before deciding whether to remove the original. See [Managing your original games](#managing-your-original-games) for more information about each option. ### 4. Start the conversion Once everything is configured, select **Start conversion**. The compressor will take care of the required file copying, LZ4 compression, AMPR runtime installation, and game-readable permissions. You can follow the progress in real time, including conversion speed and estimated remaining time. These estimates reflect the steps selected for your particular conversion. If something needs attention before starting, the interface will explain what's missing beneath the Start conversion button. ### 5. Verify and finish **Content verification is enabled by default**, and it's recommended to leave it on. Verification checks the converted content for data integrity before the compressor performs any requested operations on the original game. You can skip verification, but the resulting game will be marked **Unverified**. A successful verification doesn't necessarily mean the game will launch or function correctly, so it's worth testing the converted game yourself. Once conversion finishes, your compressed game will be saved to the selected location. If you enabled **Restart ShadowMount after conversion**, the compressor will also restart ShadowMount to refresh its game library. ## Using the app from more than one device Open the same PS5 IP address and port on each device. Game selection, destination folders, compression level, verification choices, original-game options, and mount state stay synchronized between browsers. A conversion keeps running on the console when you close a browser. Opening the interface on another device shows the current stage, game, file, transfer speeds, elapsed time, estimated remaining time, and progress. Setup and Progress tab selection stays local to each browser. ## Managing your original games You don't necessarily have to keep two copies of every game. The compressor provides several options for organizing your storage after a successful conversion. | Option | What happens | |---|---| | **Keep both** | Your original game stays untouched, and the compressed game is saved to your chosen destination. | | **Delete original** | The original is permanently removed once the selected conversion checks have completed successfully. You'll be asked to confirm this choice. | | **Move original** | The original game is moved to another folder or drive after conversion. | | **Swap original and converted** | The compressed game takes the original game's place, while the original is relocated to the destination drive. | Folder dumps currently use **Keep both**. Moving, deleting, and swapping the original are available for image sources. ### Moving games between drives When moving an original game to another drive, the compressor copies and verifies it before removing the old file. This helps protect against data loss during transfers. The original game is unmounted before any operation that requires moving or deleting its image. ### Swapping game locations The **Swap original and converted** option is useful when you want the compressed version to remain on your main game drive while keeping the original on another drive. For example, you could compress a game from your internal SSD to a USB drive, then swap their locations so the compressed game ends up on the internal SSD and the original moves to USB. Swapping is only available when the original and conversion destination are on different drives. Because the process temporarily requires additional copies, both drives must have sufficient free space. Full conversion and returned-copy verification are required. **Important:** Swapping is not an atomic operation. If it's interrupted, successfully copied files are preserved rather than automatically removed. You may need to review the resulting folders manually. ### Customizing folders All folder settings are grouped under **Destination folders**: - **Converted Game Folder:** Where the new compressed game is initially saved. - **Original Game Folder:** Where the original is moved when using Move or Swap. - **Final Converted Game Folder:** Where the converted game is placed on the original drive when swapping. Only the folder options relevant to your selected operation are enabled. ## Compression settings The compressor uses **LZ4 HC** compression, with level **7** selected by default. LZ4 is designed for fast decompression, making it suitable for game assets that need to be accessed while playing. Actual storage savings depend on the game and its contents. Conversions use a multithreaded pipeline with a maximum of eight threads, including the coordinator. Most users can leave the default compression and verification settings unchanged. ## Canceling a conversion You can cancel a conversion while it's running. When canceling, the interface lets you choose whether to keep or delete the partially generated output. Keeping it may be useful for inspection, but an incomplete conversion should not be treated as a playable game. If a conversion fails, the compressor won't proceed with the selected move, delete, or swap operation on the original game. Failed or canceled jobs may still leave partial or completed folders behind. Check the locations reported by the interface before attempting another conversion. ## Things to know LZ4 Game Compressor is currently **beta software**. Although it includes storage checks and content verification, there are a few things worth keeping in mind: - **Compression results vary.** Games containing already-compressed assets may see smaller reductions in size. - **Verification isn't a compatibility test.** A verified conversion can still encounter issues when launching or playing. - **Keep a backup when possible.** Especially when trying a game for the first time. - **Deleting is permanent.** If you choose to remove your original, make sure you're comfortable relying on the converted copy. - **Interrupted operations may need cleanup.** In particular, moving or swapping games between drives can leave extra copies if the process doesn't finish. For the safest experience, start with **Keep both**, leave verification enabled, and test your compressed game before deleting the original. ## License and acknowledgments LZ4 Game Compressor is distributed under the **GPL-3.0-or-later** license. It incorporates licensed AMPR format, runtime, and packing code from [ampr_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/ampr_emu), along with third-party components including LZ4, PicoSHA2, nlohmann/json, and toml++. Additional information is available in: - [Credits and third-party acknowledgments](CREDITS.md) - [License](LICENSE) - [Source provenance](docs/PROVENANCE.md) - [Build instructions](docs/BUILD.md) When redistributing the application, preserve the applicable license notices and provide corresponding source code as required by the respective licenses. No game content or proprietary Sony SDK is included. ## Reporting a problem Choose **Report issue** in the app, enter a title and describe what happened. The report includes images of Setup and Progress, detected games and storage, dropdown choices, settings, compressor logs and ShadowMount’s debug log. Only the app interface is captured. Game names and file paths may appear in the report; game contents are not uploaded. Large logs include the last 1 MiB and are marked when truncated. Review the image previews or choose **Review report** to inspect the complete report. Check the consent box and choose **Send private report**. Reports go through the project’s Supabase service to a private GitHub repository accessible to its owner and any collaborators they authorize. No GitHub login is needed. If submission fails, save the report and retry later.

latestRelease.body:
# LZ4 Game Compressor beta.7

Private reports now include ShadowMount’s debug log when available, alongside the compressor diagnostics and app tab images. This helps investigate game-launch and mount failures.

The app reads /data/shadowmount/debug.log only; it does not enable logging or change ShadowMount settings. The report review includes its contents, availability, original size and whether it was truncated. Large logs include the last 1 MiB. Reports can include game names, paths and crash details and require your consent before sending privately.

Update through Updates → Check for updates → Install and restart. After reproducing a problem, use Report issue to submit a fresh report.

This beta converts only mountable PS5 game images and extracted folder dumps. Keep backups; verification does not guarantee launch compatibility.

repos.readme:
🚀 PS5 FFPFSC PRO

PS5 Game Compression Utility

📥 Download • 📺 YouTube • ☕ Ko-fi

--- ## 📦 About PS5 FFPFSC PRO is a cross-platform GUI for compressing PlayStation 5 game dumps using MkPFS and FFPFSC. The application supports Windows, Linux, and macOS. The goal is simple: make PS5 game compression easy without requiring command-line tools or complicated setup. Whether you're compressing a single game, batch processing multiple titles, or browsing community compatibility reports, everything can be done from one interface. --- ## 🖼️ Screenshots ### Main Window ![PS5 FFPFSC PRO Main Window](screenshots/main-window.png) ### Community Compatibility Database ![Community Database](screenshots/community-database.png) ### Compression Progress ![Compression Progress](screenshots/compression-progress.png) --- ## ✨ Features * Compress PS5 game dumps into .ffpfsc * Supports game folders, .exfat, .ffpkg, .zip, .rar, and .7z * Drag-and-drop support * Batch compression * Multi-image queueing * Compression tuning options * Compression presets (Fast, Balanced, Max Compression, Low RAM) * Automatic update checker * Live RAM meter * Automatic retry on out-of-memory errors * Detailed logs and progress tracking * Per-game output folders * Compact mode * Interactive feature tour * What's New dialog after updates * Community Compatibility Database * APR / AMPR game support --- ## 📂 Supported Inputs * PS5 game folders * `.exfat` images * `.ffpkg` images * `.zip` archives * `.rar` archives * `.7z` archives --- ## 🌐 Community Compatibility Database After a successful compression, you can optionally submit your results to the community database. The database allows users to: * Share compatibility reports * Report Working / Partial / Not Working / Not Tested Yet status * Search by game name * Search by Title ID * View report counts * View ShadowMount version information * Browse compatibility reports directly from the application * Duplicate submission protection * Vote-based reporting system * Submit results directly from the application * Filter by compatibility status * Browse over 5,000+ community compatibility reports Compatibility status is vote-based so one incorrect report cannot override community results. View the live compatibility database: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1dgu0p7U2yB_mhcUELz-Wkc7Yhs-avoWLY1Gcm0n5XJw/edit?usp=drive_web&ouid=115958744890792485831 Or access it directly from PS5 FFPFSC PRO. --- ## ⚙️ Compression Tuning Advanced users can fine-tune compression using: * Compression level selection * CPU core selection * Block size selection Available block sizes: * Auto * Auto-Fit * 16384 * 32768 * 65536 Smaller block sizes may improve results for games containing large numbers of small files. Compression Presets * 🚀 Fast * ⚖️ Balanced * 🗜️ Max Compression * 💾 Low RAM Presets automatically configure compression level, CPU cores, and block size. --- ## 🎮 AMPR / APR Support PS5 FFPFSC PRO can detect games that require the AMPR emulator. Features include: * Automatic PlayGo chunk detection * Automatic APR title detection * Automatic AMPR index generation * Dedicated AMPR folder configuration * Compatibility reporting support * Batch mode support --- 📊 Monitoring & Automation * Live RAM meter * Automatic update checking * Windows completion notifications * Automatic retry on memory errors * Real-time progress tracking --- 🎓 User Experience * Interactive feature tour * What's New dialog after updates * Full Help / FAQ section * Detailed logging * Resizable log panel * Compact mode --- ## 🚀 Getting Started 1. Download the latest release. 2. Run `PS5_FFPFSC_PRO.exe` 3. Add a game folder, archive, `.exfat`, or `.ffpkg` image. 4. Select your compression settings. 5. Click **Start**. The application handles the rest. --- ## 🛠️ Common Issues ### Out of Memory Try: * Lowering CPU cores * Lowering compression level * Closing other applications ### Disk Full Ensure sufficient free space exists in both: * Output folder * Temporary folder ### Write Errors Verify that: * Output locations are valid * Drives are writable * Storage devices have enough free space The application provides detailed error messages and recommended fixes whenever possible. --- ## 🙏 Credits ### Compression Backend * MkPFS * Bizkut ### Community Special thanks to everyone testing games, submitting compatibility reports, reporting bugs, and helping improve the project. --- ## 🔗 Links 📺 YouTube https://youtube.com/@KINGDKAK ☕ Ko-fi https://ko-fi.com/KINGDKAK 📥 Releases https://github.com/KINGDKAK/PS5-FFPFSC-PRO/releases --- ## ⚠️ Disclaimer This project is provided as-is. Only use content you legally own and follow all applicable laws in your region. --- ⭐ If you find the project useful, consider starring the repository and contributing compatibility reports to help the community.
